analysis.investment_thesis: Kitex Garments fails both legs of the Magic Formula: Earnings Yield of ~4.5% (EBIT 201 Cr / EV ~4,476 Cr) is well below my 6% minimum, and ROCE of 10.2% is below my 12% floor. With current operating margins actually negative (-2.58% TTM) and FCF burning -451 Cr in FY25, there is no quantifiable "good business at a cheap price" here today.
key_strengths: FY25 revenue recovered to 983 Cr (+59% YoY) and operating income bounced to 201 Cr, showing the core export business can generate real earnings
Dominant infant/childrenswear niche with established US export relationships provides some demand visibility
Forward P/E of 9.07 implies market expects a large earnings step-up once new capacity is absorbed
key_risks: Massive debt surge: borrowings rocketed from 0 (FY21) to 1,184 Cr (FY25), debt/equity now 0.98 — interest burden will compress EBIT
FCF deeply negative three straight years: -121 Cr, -655 Cr, -451 Cr; CWIP ballooned to 1,283 Cr — capital not yet earning returns
Current TTM operating margin is -2.58%, meaning the Magic Formula literally cannot be applied — EBIT is near zero or negative on a trailing basis
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 71.82x — extremely expensive on any trailing earnings basis
Nine-year EBITDA CAGR of only 0.4% despite revenue growing 6.8% CAGR — the business has not compounded earnings
Highly volatile profits: 110→83→64→103→54→125→57→56→136 Cr — no predictable earnings power, a Magic Formula requirement
Negative current operating margin contradicts FY25 annual data, suggesting recent-quarter deterioration post the best FY25 quarter
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Through the Magic Formula lens, Kitex is uninvestable today. Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) = 201 Cr / 4,476 Cr ≈ 4.5% — well below my 6% hurdle, let alone the 12%+ I want. ROCE of 10.2% is below my 12% floor, and the current TTM operating margin of -2.58% means trailing EBIT is functionally zero or negative, making the formula uncomputable on the most recent data. Both pillars of the Magic Formula — cheap AND good — are absent simultaneously.

The investment "thesis" here is entirely a construction story: CWIP went from 12 Cr in FY22 to 1,283 Cr in FY25, funded by 1,184 Cr of new debt. If the new capacity delivers the earnings implied by the 9x forward P/E (~378 Cr net profit vs. 136 Cr in FY25), the stock becomes interesting — but that is a speculative bet on execution, not a Magic Formula buy. Until capacity translates into high ROIC on the expanded asset base, this is a capital-intensive story with no current earnings yield to anchor valuation. I would revisit only when EBIT/EV crosses 10%+ and ROCE is demonstrably above 15% on the full deployed capital base.
